keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1301-1302: Firoz Shah's accession year. 'Lakhnauti extended from at least the rivers Son and Ghogra in the west to Sylhet in the east'; 'the north boundary was Dinajpur-Rangpur, and the south boundary included Hughli and the Sundarbans'; Satgaon 'was completed during the time of Firuz Shah'; 'He built a mint at Sonargaon'. All three are undated inside his reign (1301-1322), so 1301 is a bridge at confidence 1. Bihar is not drawn as Bengal's but as a contested zone (ledger).

ledger.note: 1287: Bughra Khan declares Bengal independent. 'After the death of Ghiyasuddin in 1287, Bughra Khan declared independence of Bengal'; governor since 1281, independent sultan 1287-1291 (lead). Mirror of mamluk-dynasty ledger 'loss 1287' ('Bughra Khan's Bengal').

region.text: Satgaon on the Hooghly and the Sundarbans, the south of Firoz Shah's kingdom

ledger.counterpart: local rulers of Satgaon and the Sundarbans (unnamed on the page)
ledger.note: 1301: Satgaon and the Sundarbans come into the kingdom. The Satgaon conquest was 'begun under Rukunuddin Kaikaus by general Zafar Khan, and was completed during the time of Firuz Shah' (reign 1301-1322); Matuk, 'a Hindu raja of the Sundarban area', was defeated in an expedition led by Sikandar Khan Ghazi. The page dates none of it; 1301 is the accession year, a bridge.

region.text: Sonargaon and the Dhaka country, the east of Firoz Shah's kingdom

ledger.note: 1301: Sonargaon and the Dhaka country come into the kingdom. 'He built a mint at Sonargaon' and Ghiyasuddin Bahadur 'also minted at Sonargaon and Ghiyaspur'; the deva-dynasty of Bikrampur, whose last dated event is 1294, held this country. The page dates no conquest; 1301 is the accession year, a bridge.

region.text: Bihar, which Firoz Shah 'held firmly against the Khaljis'

ledger.note: 1301 (bridge): Firoz Shah holds Bihar against the Delhi Khaljis. 'He held Bihar firmly against the Khaljis,' shown by two inscriptions found in Bihar, and 'entrusted the governorship of Bihar to Tajuddin Hatim Khan'. No campaign is dated; Bihar is drawn contested, not owned, because the khalji-dynasty (Delhi) dossier's shapes keep part of it.

ledger.counterpart: rulers of Sylhet (unnamed on the page)
ledger.note: 1303: Firoz Shah conquers Sylhet. 'According to an inscription Firuz Shah conquered Sylhet in 1303 CE'; Shah Jalal and Syed Nasiruddin are associated with the conquest.

region.text: Bihar, which Firoz Shah 'held firmly against the Khaljis'

ledger.note: 1320 (bridge): the Khalji dynasty of Delhi falls, ending the Khalji-Bengal contest for Bihar (khalji-dynasty dossier: dissolve 1320). The page says only that Firuz 'held Bihar firmly against the Khaljis'.

region.text: Bengal as Cliopatria's Tughlaq 1326 shape holds it (the tughlaq-dynasty dossier's region)

ledger.note: 1324: Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq turns on Bengal. 'In 1324, Tughluq turned his attention towards Bengal, then in the midst of a civil war' (Shamsuddin Firoz Shah had died in 1322 at Khulna). Mirror of tughlaq-dynasty ledger 4.

region.text: Bengal as Cliopatria's Tughlaq 1326 shape holds it (the tughlaq-dynasty dossier's region)

ledger.note: 1325: the Bengal campaign ends. Tughluq died at Kara-Manikpur in February 1325; before that, 'On his way back to Delhi, he fought and defeated the Raja of Tirhut (north Bihar) and annexed his territory'. Mirror of tughlaq-dynasty ledger 5.

region.text: Bengal as Cliopatria's Tughlaq 1326 shape holds it (the tughlaq-dynasty dossier's region)

ledger.note: 1325: Bengal passes to Delhi. 'After victory, he placed Nasiruddin on the throne of West Bengal as a vassal state, and East Bengal was annexed.' Mirror of tughlaq-dynasty ledger 6, which draws all of Bengal as annexed; the vassal throne in the west is not drawn.

notes: No Cliopatria row and no Wikipedia article of its own (the Bughra Khan, Firoz Shah and Bengal Sultanate pages cover it); the slug is the mamluk-dynasty and tughlaq-dynasty dossiers'. DYNASTY: no page opened names a dynasty; 'Balbani' is the mamluk-dynasty dossier's word, and the Firoz Shah page says only that an old theory made him Balban's grandson and that he 'called himself only Sultan', so continuity between Bughra Khan's line (Kaikaus from 1291) and Firoz Shah (1301-1322) is assumed; 1291-1301 is undescribed. LAND: 1287-1300 is the Mamluk 1285 outline inside Bengal; the Firoz Shah gains are bridged to his accession year (1301), the Sylhet conquest to 1303 (the one dated event); Chittagong is left out (conquered 1340, Bengal Sultanate page); Bihar is a contest, not a possession. The Khalji (Delhi) dossier takes Bengal out of every Khalji shape but leaves 227 Bihar cells in the 1294-1320 shapes, which is why Bihar is a contest zone. Deva dynasty (Bikrampur) held the Dhaka country until its last dated event of 1294 (deva-dynasty dossier): 1295-1300 is nobody's land by design. AFTER 1325: Nasiruddin's vassal throne in West Bengal and the three-way split are the tughlaq-dynasty dossier's to describe. RULERS: Bughra Khan 1287-1291, Kaikaus from 1291, Firoz Shah 1301-1322 are on the pages; Shihabuddin, Ghiyasuddin Bahadur, Nasiruddin Ibrahim have no reign years; no ruler strip. Gazetteer names needed: Lakhnauti (Gaur), Satgaon, Sonargaon (places).
